Rashi on Ketubot 59b:10:1.hebrew: שומטת דד מפיו - לא תניקנו, שחל הנדר. אלמא לא משעבדא ליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:10:1.english: She removes [her] nipple from his mouth - She must not nurse him, for the vow has taken effect. Thus, she is not obligated to him.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:10:2.english: He compels her, and she nurses [him] - Because she is obligated to him, and [therefore] the vow does not take effect.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:10:3.english: If he recognized her - [Meaning] that he does not want to nurse from another [woman].

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:11:1.english: Here, with what are we dealing - [in] the baraita.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:12:1.hebrew: ונפלגו בכתובה בעלמא - נדרה מליהנות לו וקיים לה, בש"א: תצא ותטול כתובה, ובה"א: תצא בלא כתובה:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:12:1.english: And let them dispute about a marriage contract in general - [If] she vowed [not] to derive benefit from him and he ratified [the vow] for her: Beit Shammai say she shall be divorced and collect [her] marriage contract, and Beit Hillel say she shall be divorced without [collecting her] marriage contract.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:12:2.english: And furthermore, it is taught - Regarding all women, and even without a vow.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:12:3.english: She does not nurse - If she does not want [to].

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:2:1.hebrew: לא דמיא אלא להא - לא דמי לשדה זו שמשכנתי לך סתם, אלא לאומר שדה זו שמשכנתי לעשר שנים, דאין בידו לפדותה ולהקדישה עכשיו:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:2:1.english: [This] is comparable only to this - It is not comparable to [the case of] "This field that I have mortgaged to you" [stated] without specification, but rather to one who says, "This field that I have mortgaged [to you] for ten years," where it is not in his power to redeem it and consecrate it now.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:2:2.english: That it is consecrated - For it is his.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:4:1.hebrew: דקדושת הגוף נינהו - כקדושת מזבח שאין להן פדיון, כך אין פדיון לקונם להיות ניתר למי שנאסר עליו, שהרי אינו הקדש גמור לתפוס פדיונו, אלא אסור על אדם אחד. וכיון דקדושת הגוף הוא, מפקיע מידי שעבוד שהיא משועבדת לבעלה, וחייל. ולקמן פריך: א"כ, מאי איריא "שמא יגרשנה"? מהשתא חייל:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:4:1.english: Since they are [a type of] inherent sanctity - Like sanctity of the altar, which has no redemption, so too there is no redemption for a konam to become permitted to the one to whom it was forbidden, for it is not complete consecration to transfer [sanctity onto] its redemption [money], rather it is forbidden to one person. And since it is inherent sanctity, it abrogates the lien by which she is subjugated to her husband, and [the konam] takes effect. And later [the Gemara] asks: If so, why [does the Mishnah] specifically [say] "lest he divorce her"? It takes effect from now!

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:4:2.hebrew: הקדש - כגון ששיעבד שורו לבעל חוב וחזר והקדישו, מפקיע שעבוד המלוה, וגובה חובו ממקום אחר, וזה כשר לקרבן ואינו גזול, דלא הוה קני ליה אלא לגוביינא בעלמא. ודוקא קדושת הגוף, אבל קדושת דמים דבדק הבית לא מפקיע שעבוד, כדתנן בערכין (דף כג:): מוסיף עוד דינר ופודה את הנכסים הללו כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:4:2.english: Consecration - For example, where one pledged his ox to a creditor and then went and consecrated it, [the consecration] abrogates the lender's lien, and [the lender] collects his debt from elsewhere, and this [ox] is fit for a sacrifice and is not [considered] stolen, because [the lender] did not acquire it except merely for collection. And [this applies] specifically [to] inherent sanctity, but monetary sanctity for the Temple treasury does not abrogate a lien, as we learned in the Mishnah in Arakhin (23b): "[He] adds another dinar and redeems these properties, etc."

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:4:3.hebrew: חמץ - עשה חמצו אפותיקי לעובד כוכבים והגיע הפסח, איסור חמץ מפקיעו משעבוד העובד כוכבים ונאסר בהנאה. והא דתנן (פסחים דף ל:) עובד כוכבים שהלוה לישראל על חמצו, אחר הפסח מותר בהנאה — אוקמינן לה התם כשהרהינו אצלו, שמסרו בידו משכון:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:4:3.english: Leavened bread - [If one] made his leavened bread designated collateral [apotiki] for a non-Jew and Passover arrived, the prohibition of leavened bread abrogates it from the non-Jew's lien, and it is forbidden for benefit. And [regarding] that which we learned in a Mishnah (Pesachim 30b): "A non-Jew who lent [money] to a Jew against his leavened bread, after Passover it is permitted for benefit" — we established it there [as referring to] when he deposited it with him, [meaning] that he handed it over into his possession as a pledge.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:4:4.hebrew: ושחרור - עשה עבדו אפותיקי, ושחררו הלוה, משוחרר, וזה גובה חובו ממקום אחר:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:4:4.english: And liberation - [If] he made his slave an apotiki [designated security for a debt] and the borrower liberated him, [the slave] is liberated, and this [creditor] collects his debt from elsewhere.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:5:1.hebrew: ונקדשו מהשתא - מאי איריא דקתני שמא יגרשנה? מהשתא נמי קדיש:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:5:1.english: And let them become consecrated from now - Why [does it] specifically teach "lest he divorce her"? From now as well, [it] becomes consecrated.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:5:2.hebrew: אלמוה רבנן לשעבודיה דבעל - בעודה תחתיו, דשויוהו רבנן כלוקח גמור ולא כמלוה:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:5:2.english: The Sages strengthened the husband's lien - while she is under his [authority], for the Sages treated him like a full buyer and not like a creditor.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:6:2.hebrew: שתים אינה מבשלת כו' - בגמרא פריך, אמאי לא איפטרה מכולהו בחדא שפחה שהכניסה במקומה:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:6:2.english: Two [maidservants], she does not cook, etc. - In the Gemara, it asks why she is not exempted from all of them with one maidservant whom she brought in her place.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:6:3.english: She sits in a chair - She does not trouble herself for him to go on an errand to bring him an object from the house to the upper story.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:8:1.hebrew: טוחנת ס"ד - המים מגלגלין האופן וטוחן:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:8:1.english: Grinds, could it enter your mind - The water turns the wheel and [it] grinds.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:8:2.hebrew: מטחנת - מכינה צורכי טחינה, נותנתו באפרכסת וקולטת הקמח:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:8:2.english: She supervises the grinding - She prepares the necessities for grinding: she puts [the grain] into the hopper [of the mill] and collects the flour.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:8:3.english: And if you wish, say - Actually, she grinds [it] herself.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:8:4.english: Of the hand - A hand mill.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:9:1.english: For a woman's ornaments - That they should buy her ornaments with which to adorn herself.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:9:2.hebrew: שיעדן - את זיוה, אישקלויי"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Ketubot 59b:9:2.english: That he will beautify - [meaning] her radiance; escloier [to brighten] in Old French.

Rashi on Ketubot 59b:9:3.english: Toward her maturity - The days of youth.

Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:11:1.hebrew: כגון שנדרה היא וקיים לה הוא - שאסרה הנאת הנקה על עצמה, שהיא נהנית בהנקה — כדאמר לקמן: "הוא אומר שלא להניק והיא אומרת להניק — שומעין לה", משום צערא דידה, וכי ההיא דשוחה עליו ומניקתו מפני הסכנה. אבל ליכא למימר דאסרה הנאת יניקתה עליו, כיון דמשעבדא ליה — אין הנדר חל. והשתא פליגי: דב"ש סברי דהוא נתן אצבע בין שיניה, הלכך אינו כופה להניק — פי', להשכיר מינקת; וב"ה סברי היא נתנה אצבע בין שיניה, וכופה להניק — שתשכיר לו מינקת או תצא בלא כתובה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:11:1.english: [A case] where she made a vow and he ratified [it] for her - That she forbade the benefit of nursing upon herself, for she derives benefit from nursing — as [the Gemara] states later: "[If] he says not to nurse and she says to nurse, we listen to her," because of her pain, and like that [case] where she bends over him and nurses him because of the danger. However, one cannot say that she forbade the benefit of her nursing upon him, [because] since she is obligated to him, the vow does not take effect. And now they disagree: for Beit Shammai hold that he placed a finger between her teeth, therefore he cannot force her to nurse — meaning, to hire a wet nurse; whereas Beit Hillel hold [that] she placed a finger between her teeth, and he can force her to nurse — [meaning] that she must hire a wet nurse for him or leave without a ketubah.

Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:1:1.hebrew: שדה זו שמשכנתי לך לכשאפדנה ממך תיקדש - משמע דבעודה ממושכנת אינו יכול להקדיש, דאין כח להקדש לבטל כח המלוה שהיא ממושכנת בידו. ותימה, דאמרי' בסוף איזהו נשך (ב"מ עג:): "רב מרי בר רחל משכן ליה עובד כוכבים ההוא ביתא, אזל עובד כוכבים זבניה לרבא, נטר תריסר ירחי שתא ושקל אגר ביתא ואמטיה לרבא כו'", אלמא הפקיע המכר כחו של רב מרי שהיה לו לדור בבית חנם שהיתה ממושכנת בידו, והפקיע המכר כחו והוצרך להעלות לו שכר לרבא. וי"ל, דאין זה הפקעת כח, אלא לפי שהיה סבור רב מרי שהיה רבא חייב לו דמי המשכנתא במקום העובד כוכבים, ולא רצה לדור בחצירו חנם משום רבית; וא"ל רבא: כדיניהם עבידנא לך, דרבא לא מיחייב ליה מידי אלא העובד כוכבים. וא"ת: והא דאמר בפ' האומר משקלי עלי (ערכין כא. ושם): "הקדישו משכיר, הדר בו מעלה שכר להקדש", ופריך: "היכי דייר ביה? הא במעילה קאי!" — דמשמע שבזמן השכירות יכול להקדישה? וי"ל, דכח שיש לשוכר אינו יכול להקדיש, אלא הוא והקדש שותפין בו, וימכר הבית ויקח זה דמי שכירות הבית והמותר להקדש; אבל הכא מיירי שמקדיש כל השדה, אף מה שאינו יכול להקדיש עכשיו. אי נמי: בהקדש ממש היה חל על שדה הממושכנת אף קודם שתפדה, והכא מיירי שאוסר בקונם על המלוה לכשיפדנה; דיכול להיות דבשדה ממושכנת אינו יכול לאוסרה בקונם, אף על פי שיכול להקדישה, כדמוכח בערכין דיכול להקדיש יותר ממה שיכול לאסור בקונם. ומתרצא בהכי האי דפריך לעיל: "ומי איכא מידי דאילו השתא לא קדיש ולקמיה קדיש?" — ומאי קשיא ליה, דלמה לא תוכל להקדיש מעשה ידיה לאחר שתתגרש? מאי שנא מנכסי מלוג שיכולה למכור עכשיו לכשתתאלמן או תתגרש? אלא ודאי, אע"פ שיכולה להקדיש מידי דהוי אמכר, לא תוכל לאסור. ועוד יכול להיות, דאפילו היתה מקדשת ידיה לשמים לגמרי, לא היה ראוי לחול הקדש כמו על שדה, משום דבשדה חל ההקדש על גוף השדה בעודה ברשות המלוה, וממילא יקדשו הפירות כשיצא הגוף מרשותו; אבל ידיה, אפי' הקדישו לשמים, אין נתפשות בהקדש, ואפילו בעבד אמר רב דגופיה לא קדיש, ובבן חורין מודו כ"ע, ולכך אפי' הקדישו לגמרי אין להקדש לחול יותר מאוסר למלוה בקונם שדה הממושכן לו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:1:1.english: "This field that I mortgaged to you will be consecrated when I redeem it from you" - This implies that while it is still mortgaged, he cannot consecrate [it], because consecration does not have the power to nullify the right of the lender in whose possession it is mortgaged. And this is astonishing, for we say at the end of [chapter] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 73b): A non-Jew mortgaged a certain house to Rav Mari bar Rachel; the non-Jew then went and sold it to Rava. [Rav Mari] waited twelve months of the year, and took the rent of the house and brought it to Rava, etc. Thus we see that the sale abrogated the right of Rav Mari—who had [the right] to dwell in the house free of charge since it was mortgaged in his possession—and the sale abrogated his right so that he had to pay rent to Rava. And one can answer that this was not an abrogation of [his] right; rather, [it was] because Rav Mari thought that Rava owed him the mortgage money in place of the non-Jew, and he did not want to dwell in his courtyard free of charge because of [the prohibition of] interest. And Rava said to him: "I am acting toward you according to their [non-Jewish] laws," for Rava did not owe him anything—rather, the non-Jew [owed him]. And if you ask: What of that which is stated in the chapter HaOmer Mishkali Alai (Arakhin 21a, and there): "If the landlord consecrated it, the one dwelling in it [the tenant] pays rent to the Temple treasury," and [the Gemara] asks: "How may he dwell in it? Surely it is subject to [the prohibition of] me'ila [misappropriation of consecrated property]!"—which implies that during the period of the lease, he can consecrate it? And one can answer that the right that the tenant possesses, he [the landlord] cannot consecrate; rather, he [the tenant] and the Temple treasury are partners in it, and the house is sold and this [tenant] takes the value of the lease of the house and the remainder [goes] to the Temple treasury. Here, however, it is speaking of where he consecrates the entire field, even that which he cannot consecrate now. Alternatively: Actual consecration [to the Temple treasury] would take effect on a mortgaged field even before it is redeemed, and here it is speaking of where he prohibits [it] with a konam [vow] to the lender for when he redeems it; for it is possible that with a mortgaged field he cannot prohibit it with a konam even though he can consecrate it [to the Temple], as is proven in Arakhin, that one can consecrate more than one can prohibit with a konam. And with this is resolved that which [the Gemara] asked above: "And is there anything that right now is not consecrated, and later becomes consecrated?"—for what was its difficulty, why should she not be able to consecrate her handiwork for after she is divorced? How is this different from melog property, which she can sell now [to take effect] when she is widowed or divorced? Rather, certainly, even though she can consecrate [it]—just as with a sale—she cannot prohibit [it with a konam]. And furthermore, it is possible that even if she were to consecrate her hands to Heaven completely, consecration would not be fit to take effect [on them] as it does on a field; because with a field, the consecration takes effect on the body of the field while it is in the lender's possession, and automatically the produce becomes consecrated when the body leaves his possession. With her hands, however, even if one consecrated them to Heaven, they are not seized by consecration—and even regarding a slave, Rav said that his body is not consecrated, and regarding a free person everyone agrees. Therefore, even if one consecrated them completely, consecration cannot take effect any more than one who prohibits to a lender with a konam a field mortgaged to him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:4:1.hebrew: קונמות קאמרת כו' - וא"ת: א"כ, כל אדם יפקיע כל ממונו מבעל חובו על ידי קונם? וי"ל: דלאו דווקא שעבוד דבעל אלמוה רבנן, אלא ה"נ דאלמוה לשעבודא דב"ח, כדמוכח בריש המדיר (לקמן כתובות ע.), דפריך: וכיון דמשועבד לה, היכי מצי מדיר לה? ולימא דמפקע שעבודה ע"י קונם! אלא ודאי דאלמוה נמי לשעבודא דאשה. וא"ת: בפ' אלמנה ביבמות (דף סו: ושם), גבי אצטלא דפרסוה אמיתנא, אמאי קאמר רבא "קנייה מיתנא"? הא אלמוה רבנן לשעבודא דאשה! וי"ל: דדוקא בקונמות אלמוה, שלא יפקיע חובו; אבל ההיא דפ' אלמנה, דנאסר לכל העולם, ליכא למיחש להכי, ומפקיע מידי שעבוד כמו הקדש. והא דאמר בהחובל (ב"ק דף צ. ושם) דעבדי מלוג אין יוצאין בשן ועין לא לאיש ולא לאשה, דאלמוה רבנן לשעבודא דבעל אע"ג דשחרור דמי להקדש — סבירא ליה לרבא בפרק אלמנה (יבמות דף סו:) כמ"ד לאשה אבל לא לאיש; א"נ, ידו עדיפא מידה כיון דאכיל פירות בחייה, כדאמרינן בהכותב (לקמן כתובות דף פג.):
Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:4:1.english: Did you speak [about] konamot, etc. - And if you ask: If so, anyone could abrogate [the lien on] all his property from his creditor by means of a konam! And one can answer: It is not specifically the husband's lien that the Rabbis reinforced, rather so too they reinforced the creditor's lien, as is proven at the beginning of [the chapter] HaMadir (below, Ketubot 70a), where [the Gemara] asks: Since he is obligated to her, how can he vow to prohibit her [from benefiting from him]? Why not say that he abrogates her lien by means of the konam! Rather, it is certain that they also reinforced the wife's lien. And if you ask: In the chapter Almanah in Yevamot (66b and there [in the parallel]), regarding a cloak that they spread over a corpse, why did Rava say, "The corpse acquired it"? Surely the Rabbis reinforced the wife's lien! And one can answer: Specifically with konamot did they reinforce [the lien], so that one should not abrogate his debt; however, [in] that [case] of the chapter Almanah, where it becomes prohibited to the entire world, there is no reason to be concerned about this, and it abrogates a lien just like consecration. And [as for] that which is stated in [the chapter] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 90a and there), that melog slaves do not go free for [the loss of] a tooth or an eye, neither for the husband nor for the wife — because the Rabbis reinforced the husband's lien even though emancipation is similar to consecration — Rava holds in the chapter Almanah (Yevamot 66b) like the one who says [that they go free] for the wife, but not for the husband. Alternatively, his [right of] possession is superior to hers, since he consumes the produce [of her property] during her lifetime, as we say in [the chapter] HaKotev (below, Ketubot 83a).

Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:4:2.english: Consecration, leavened bread, and liberation - I have written [about this] in [the chapter] HaSholeach (Gittin 40b and there).

Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:6:1.hebrew: ארבע יושבת בקתדרא - אע"ג דבשלש נמי אינה עושה מכל מלאכות שהוזכרו במשנה, מכל מקום עושה מלאכות קטנות שבבית שלא הוזכרו במשנה, ואיכא נמי ארחי ופרחי דבגמרא; וכי הכניסה לו ד' אינה עושה כלום:
Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:6:1.english: Four — she sits in a chair [katedra] - Even though with three [maidservants] as well she does not perform any of the tasks that were mentioned in the Mishnah, nevertheless she performs minor household tasks that were not mentioned in the Mishnah, and there are also [the tasks for] wayfarers [mentioned] in the Gemara; whereas when she brought him four [maidservants], she does nothing [at all].

Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:8:1.hebrew: טוחנת ס"ד - הא דתנן בהניזקין (גיטין סא:): "אשת חבר טוחנת עם אשת עם הארץ", לא פריך "טוחנת ס"ד?" — דדוקא הכא פריך, דאתא לאשמועינן "אלו מלאכות שהאשה עושה", דקאי אעיקר מלאכה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:8:1.english: "Grinds — could it enter your mind?!" - Regarding that which we learned in [the chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 61b): "The wife of a chaver may grind with the wife of an am ha'aretz," [the Gemara there] does not ask, "[Could it] enter your mind [that she] grinds?" For specifically here [the Gemara] asks [this], because [the Mishnah] comes to teach us "these are the labors that a wife performs," which refers to the primary labor [itself].

Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:9:1.hebrew: תני רבי חייא אין אשה אלא ליופי - לא פליג אלא אטוחנת ואופה ומניקה את בנה וכיוצא בהן, שמכחישות יופיה; אבל אעושה בצמר לא פליג, דמעשה ידיה תחת מזונות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 59b:9:1.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches: "A wife is only for beauty" - [He] disagrees only regarding grinding, baking, nursing her child, and the like, which diminish her beauty; however, regarding working in wool he does not disagree, for her handiwork is in exchange for [her] sustenance.
